title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Tokaj and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show Tokaji, the style, Aszú, Szamorodni, Eszencia or dry Furmint, sometimes puttonyos, 5 or 6, the vintage, the producer and often a vineyard, dűlő. Késői szüretelésű means late harvest, a lighter sweet style. Tokaji Aszú usually comes in a 50 cl bottle.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Tokaji Aszú suits foie gras, blue cheese, apricot tarts and fruit desserts; its acidity also works with spicy Asian food and Hungarian dishes with paprika. Dry Furmint suits fish, poultry, pork and goose. Dry Szamorodni suits nuts and aged cheese, like a Sherry. Serve sweet wines at 10 to 12 degrees.
steps.highlight: Foie gras, blue cheese, apricot tart

steps.explanation: Rich foie gras suits Aszú's sweetness and acidity.

steps.body: An open bottle of Tokaji Aszú keeps for weeks in the fridge, thanks to its sugar and acidity.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show the style, puttonyos and vineyard
Aszú suits foie gras and fruit desserts
Dry Furmint suits fish, poultry and pork
